name: al-Buhturi
bio: Abu Ubada al-Walid ibn Ubayd al-Ta'i was born in Manbij, between Aleppo and the Euphrates, in 206 AH (821 CE). He went to Iraq and served a line of caliphs, beginning with al-Mutawakkil, then returned to Syria. With Abu Tammam and al-Mutanabbi he is one of the three counted the greatest poets of their time, and his verse was called “chains of gold”; asked which of the three was the best, Abu al-Ala' al-Ma'arri answered that al-Mutanabbi and Abu Tammam were sages, and the poet was al-Buhturi. He also compiled an anthology, the Hamasa, on the model of Abu Tammam's. He died in Manbij in 284 AH (898 CE).
